subject: Quantis Health discovery — SDK streaming & rerank fit
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Anoop Sharma <anoop@quantishealth.com>, Natalie Greene <ngreene@quantishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Quantis Health discovery — SDK streaming & rerank fit

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment.

Key customer pain points we heard
- Unpredictable inference latency on current provider (p95 ~420ms for search route) causing poor UX
- High per-token cost at current volume (approx 1.2M tokens/day) — need 25-40% unit cost reduction
- Need deterministic, structured outputs for clinical data capture (JSON schema enforcement)
- Requirement for streaming partial responses in the UI (typeahead + streaming) and function calling for several backend ops
- Want to add an embedding+rerank pipeline for search relevance with offline embedding store

Goals / success criteria
- Reduce p95 latency for search/generation routes to <150ms
- Cut per-token serving cost by ~30% via batching/quantization/caching
- Deliver stable structured outputs (strict schema) and reliable function calling for the client app
- Prototype embedding + reranker POC within 4 weeks

Integration notes
- Quantis uses Node (TypeScript) for backend and React for frontend — they'll prefer an SDK-first approach
- Primary routes: streaming user-facing responses, function calls to run data enrichment, embeddings for daily index updates

Next steps
1) I attached discovery notes and a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — Quantis-Discovery-Notes.pdf, Quantis-MAP-v1.xlsx
2) Schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive with Markus (solutions eng) to go over SDK integration and streaming samples — propose Tue 2026-05-12 10:00 PT
3) We'll scope a 4-week POC (lighting: dev -> small canary traffic) and share a cost ballpark in the MAP

Thanks — I'll get the MAP updated with timelines once we lock the deep-dive.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
Attachments: Quantis-Discovery-Notes.pdf (summary), Quantis-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP draft)

From: Anoop Sharma <anoop@quantishealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Greene <ngreene@quantishealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T18:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Quantis Health discovery — SDK streaming & rerank fit

Thanks, Soojin — helpful recap.

A few clarifications from our side:
- Current baseline: p95 ~420ms for search route when we hit our peak queries. Our users are highly sensitive to latency spikes.
- Token volume: ~1.2M/day; illustrating cost is critical for our CFO.
- For streaming: we need partial tokens as they arrive in the UI for a typeahead experience. Also important: idempotent function calls so retries don't create duplicate records.
- Embeddings: we plan to store 1536-dim vectors in our existing vector store (Pinecone). We need guidance on embedding refresh cadence and delta-updates.

Security/compliance note: before we proceed to a POC, procurement will want a SOC 2 questionnaire and a list of data retention controls. If you can share the security questionnaire or point me to the artifacts, that will speed approval.

For the deep-dive, Tue 10am PT works for Natalie and me. Can Markus demo streaming SDK samples for TypeScript and show the function-calling flow?

Regards,
Anoop
Anoop Sharma
Director, Product Engineering
Quantis Health
anoop@quantishealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Anoop Sharma <anoop@quantishealth.com>, Natalie Greene <ngreene@quantishealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Quantis Health discovery — SDK streaming & rerank fit

On Sun, May 10, 2026 at 6:40 PM Anoop Sharma <anoop@quantishealth.com> wrote:
> For streaming: we need partial tokens as they arrive in the UI for a typeahead experience. Also important: idempotent function calls so retries don't create duplicate records.

Thanks for the details — below are clarifications and what we'll bring to the deep-dive.

Short answers
- Streaming: supported by Redwood SDK (Node/TS) via chunked SSE or WebSocket transports. We'll bring a working TypeScript sample that demonstrates partial-token streaming + reconnection behavior.
- Function calling: supported with schema validation and strong idempotency hooks (we recommend an idempotency key pattern on the client). Markus will show an example of a function-calling flow that returns structured JSON and status codes.
- Embeddings: recommended model produces 1536-dim vectors (we also have 768-dim options if you want smaller vectors). For 1.2M tokens/day, we typically recommend delta-updates nightly with incremental re-embed for changed records.
- Cost reduction levers: continuous batching at the router, prefix + KV caching, and int8/4-bit quantized model variants for non-critical routes. We'll propose concrete config in the MAP.

What we'll bring to the deep-dive
- TypeScript streaming SDK sample and a short patch showing how to wire function calls (redwood-sdk-streaming-sample.patch)
- A one-page POC plan with milestones and success metrics
- A security artifacts pointer (SOC 2 report summary + data retention controls link) — Marking as pre-read in the Drive folder.

Proposed meeting: Tue 2026-05-12 10:00 PT — Markus will demo SDK examples; Marissa will outline the POC deliverables.

I attached the MAP draft again and a small SDK sample patch. If that time works we'll send a calendar invite with dial-in and a short agenda.

Best,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
Attachments: Quantis-MAP-v1.xlsx, redwood-sdk-streaming-sample.patch

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: POC plan + eng owners for Quantis

Internal note — not sent to Quantis.

POC proposal (4 weeks)
Week 0: kickoff, access, map success metrics (UX owner: Natalie), security kickoff (procurement asks)
Week 1: SDK integration + streaming demo (owner: Markus) — get TypeScript sample wired into a sandbox front-end
Week 2: Embedding pipeline + reranker stub (owner: Dev Patel) — nightly delta updates to Pinecone
Week 3: Canary can be run against 5% of traffic with monitoring (owner: Monica Patel) — latency & cost dashboards
Milestones & exit criteria
- p95 latency < 200ms on canary routes
- Structured output validation passing >= 95% of test prompts
- Embedding refresh completes within 1 hour nightly

Notes: recommend recommending 4-bit quantized variant for the reranker route initially to save cost, run A/B vs FP16 on a small sample. I can draft an SOW after the technical deep-dive.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
